meta.description: Performs gene-level association from GWAS summary statistics via genetically predicted tissue expression using FUSION, PrediXcan, S-PrediXcan, S-MultiXcan, UTMOST, MOSTWAS, kTWAS, EpiXcan, TIGAR-V2, and probabilistic fine-mapping with FOCUS and MA-FOCUS. Use when running TWAS from GWAS sumstats, prioritising candidate causal genes, picking single-tissue vs cross-tissue models, identifying LD-induced false positives, choosing ancestry-matched weights, fine-mapping co-regulated TWAS hits, or triangulating TWAS with cis-eQTL MR and colocalization.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOIs/PMIDs, p-values, or effect sizes across any of the 7 outputs. Every real execution this session matched planted ground truth exactly (FUSION JOINT.P=6e-13 for the true-signal gene, COND.P=0.63 for the null gene; a real pyfocus-schema FOCUS DB built from scratch this session recovered pips_pop1=1.0 for the true gene and ~3.4e-08 for the null-model row).

practice_boundaries.detail: Population-level gene-prioritization scope maintained throughout; unaffected by this session's fixes. Input 7's adversarial 'confirmed causal gene' framing is correctly refused per the Skill's own HLA-exclusion rule (reused from the pre-fix audit; code path untouched by the fix).

methodological_ground.detail: SKILL.md still explicitly requires triangulation (MR + coloc + FOCUS) before a causal claim and documents the HLA long-range-LD confound; unaffected by this session's fixes.

code_usability.detail: 6 of 7 inputs' code now runs end-to-end with correct, ground-truth-verified output, up from 5/7 pre-fix (FUSION.post_process.R's single-SNP crash is now fully and independently re-verified fixed on a fresh fixture; the Windows MA-FOCUS drive-letter caveat is now documented and the relative-path workaround verified end-to-end for a real 3-population run). Input 3 (FOCUS fine-mapping) still fails end-to-end under the exact documented pandas<2.2+setuptools<81 pin and np.warnings patch: building a real pyfocus-schema weight DB this session (closing the gap the fixer flagged as unexercised) surfaced two further pandas-version incompatibilities inside pyfocus's own finemap.py (DataFrame.pivot() positional args, DataFrame.append() removal) that block the actual PIP-computation step. Each is a one-line, clearly diagnosable third-party dependency-version fix (confirmed by patching and re-running, which then produced correct PIP output matching ground truth) -- resolvable, not unrunnable/logically-broken code as authored by the Skill itself, so this remains PASS rather than a veto fire, but it is a real, still-open P1, not merely a fixture-schema gap as previously framed.

functional_suitability.note: SKILL.md's own authored content remains complete and correct; both crash modes fixed this session were dependency-version issues in wrapped tools (FUSION's fusion_twas, pyfocus), not gaps in the Skill's own content -- reconfirmed independently this session.

recommendations.title: pyfocus pandas<2.2 pin+patch is insufficient to reach real FOCUS PIP output
recommendations.problem: Once a real pyfocus-schema FOCUS weight DB is used (rather than the wrong-schema DB that masked this during the fix's own verification), `focus finemap` reaches the 'Calculating PIPs' step and crashes with `TypeError: DataFrame.pivot() takes 1 positional argument but 4 were given`, and after that is worked around, with `AttributeError: 'DataFrame' object has no attribute 'append'` -- both inside pyfocus's own finemap.py, not the Skill's authored content.
recommendations.root_cause: pyfocus/finemap.py:1012 calls `attr_tmp.pivot("model_id", "attr_name", "value")` (positional args, removed by pandas>=2.0) and finemap.py:188 calls `df.append(null_dict, ignore_index=True)` (removed by pandas>=2.0). The pandas<2.2 pin only prevents the earlier delim_whitespace/np.warnings crashes; it does not avoid these because pandas<2.0 pins were never applied, and pyfocus's own code was never updated for pandas>=2.0's stricter API.
recommendations.fix: Document two further one-line patches in SKILL.md's Tool Install Notes: `attr_tmp.pivot(index="model_id", columns="attr_name", values="value")` at finemap.py:1012, and replace `df.append(null_dict, ignore_index=True)` with `pd.concat([df, pd.DataFrame([null_dict])], ignore_index=True)` at finemap.py:188. Both were confirmed this session: with both patches, focus finemap produces correct real PIP output (pips_pop1=1.0 for a true gene, ~3.4e-08 for the null-model row).

recommendations.title: `focus import ... fusion` (the Skill's own documented custom-DB route) has an undocumented mygene+rpy2 dependency, and rpy2 needs R built as a shared library
recommendations.problem: Following SKILL.md's own documented `focus import custom_panel.pos fusion --tissue ... --output ...` command fails silently (0 genes imported, no error surfaced to the user) unless `mygene` and `rpy2` are separately installed; even then, rpy2 requires R compiled as a shared library (`R was not built as a library`), which the standard R distribution referenced elsewhere in this Skill's own tooling is not.
recommendations.root_cause: pyfocus's import submodule imports mygene/rpy2 lazily and only logs an ERROR-level message rather than raising, so a user following the documented command gets an apparently-successful but empty database with no indication why.
recommendations.fix: Document the mygene+rpy2 (and R-as-shared-library) requirement in Tool Install Notes, or document the workaround used this session: build the DB directly via pyfocus's own SQLAlchemy schema (`pyfocus.models.db.load_db`/`build_model`) for a custom panel, bypassing `focus import`'s gene-symbol-lookup step entirely.
